title: One Subscriber, Two Regional Accounts
scenario_text: Bjornstad Telecom operates separate regional billing systems and a fraud-and-loyalty audit flagged a possible duplicate subscriber. The North region CRM has customer N-33120 "Erik Solberg," mobile line, national ID ending 4471, DOB 1990-11-02, personal email erik.solberg@fastmail.no, address in Tromso, loyalty tier Gold (since 2019). The South region CRM has customer S-88044 "Erik Solberg," broadband line, national ID ending 4471, DOB 1990-11-02, personal email erik.solberg@fastmail.no, address in Kristiansand (recorded after a relocation in 2023), loyalty tier Bronze (created 2023). The two systems never shared a key, so each region minted its own customer ID. Both records share the identical national ID (ending 4471), DOB, and personal email; the addresses differ only because the subscriber moved from the North to the South region. A retention offer requires the subscriber's true loyalty tenure, which should reflect the earliest continuous relationship across regions rather than the newer regional record. The audit must decide whether N-33120 and S-88044 are the same person and, if so, which loyalty start date represents the subscriber's true tenure. The retention team cannot extend the tenure-based offer until the two regional records are confirmed as one subscriber, and the North and South systems will not be technically merged until a later data-platform project, so the audit must make the determination manually. Provide that loyalty start year.
question: If the two regional records are the same subscriber, what loyalty start year represents the subscriber's true tenure?
